review_notes: I read the whole file and the related Geachean.lean and Geach.lean definitions. I also grepped the sibling Hilbert/*.lean files for how `Geachean.*_def` is used. The file has no @[simp] declarations of its own. The only simp interface issue I found is the duplicated unfold-and-simp call with local-only orientation lemmas. The `*_def` lemmas are used in both directions elsewhere, so they should not be tagged @[simp]. This is a low-severity finding. I did not run Lean, so I cannot say whether the replacement compiles. The proof of the proposed lemma may need the same `Geachean` unfolding as the current simp call.

findings.excerpt:
unfold ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass MultiGeacheanConfluentFrameClass MultiGeachean;
    simp [Geachean.reflexive_def, Geachean.euclidean_def];
findings.problem: Both `sound` and `complete` repeat the same block: `unfold` three definitions, then `simp` with the orientation lemmas `reflexive_def` and `euclidean_def`. These lemmas rewrite the named properties `Std.Refl` and `Euclidean` into `Geachean` form. They are deliberately not @[simp], because Geach.lean uses `reflexive_def` in the reverse direction (`←Geachean.reflexive_def`). So there is no canonical simp rule for the frame-class equation `ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass = MultiGeacheanConfluentFrameClass {⟨0,0,1,0⟩, ⟨1,1,0,1⟩}`. Each use has to re-derive it by unfolding and running simp with a hand-picked lemma set. The same pattern is copied into KT, S4, KTB, KT4B, Triv and other sibling files. This makes the proofs depend on the exact shape of the unfolded set-membership goal and on `simp` normalising the pair `{a, b}` into a conjunction.
findings.proposed_change: State the frame-class identity once, in this file or next to the Geach definitions. For example, add `lemma ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass_eq_multiGeachean : ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass = MultiGeacheanConfluentFrameClass {⟨0,0,1,0⟩, ⟨1,1,0,1⟩}`, and prove it once with the current `unfold … simp [reflexive_def, euclidean_def]` script. Then replace the two bullets in `sound` and `complete` by `exact` of this lemma (or its symm). Do not tag `reflexive_def` or `euclidean_def` as @[simp], since they are used in both orientations.
findings.benefit: The unfold-and-simp proof appears once instead of twice in this file. Downstream proofs no longer depend on the orientation lemmas and the exact simp normal form of the `{a, b}` membership. The simp-set change that would break them is localised to one proof.
